channel.title: Find Your Supplement Blog
channel.description: Evidence-based guides to supplements, vitamins, and nutrition science from Find Your Supplement.

item.title: Can You Actually Boost Your Immune System? The 4 Supplements With Real Evidence (and Their Limits)
item.description: Looking for the best supplements to boost your immune system before cold season? This evidence-based review sorts vitamin D, vitamin C, zinc, and probiotics by what the trials actually show, the doses studied, the safe upper limits, and who is most likely to benefit.

item.title: L-Theanine vs Magnesium for Sleep: Which One Fits Your Kind of Bad Night?
item.description: L-theanine vs magnesium for sleep comes down to why you are still awake: a mind that will not switch off, or a diet running low on a key mineral. This evidence-based review weighs the newest research on both, the doses actually tested, and when neither is the answer.

item.title: Vitamins With Food or on an Empty Stomach? The Timing Rules That Change What You Absorb
item.description: The same supplement can deliver a third more or a lot less depending on what is on your plate. This evidence-based guide sorts which nutrients need fat, which need an empty stomach, and which just need food to spare your stomach - with the exact timing cheat sheet.

item.title: Brittle, Ridged, or Peeling Nails? The Deficiencies Your Hands Are Trying to Show You
item.description: Splitting, peeling, or spoon-shaped nails can be a six-month record of a nutrient shortfall — or just what dish soap does to keratin. This evidence-based guide covers which deficiencies genuinely show up in nails, the one supplement with real trial data, and what no capsule will fix.

item.title: Does Coffee Block Your Supplements? What Caffeine Does to Iron, Calcium, and Your Multivitamin
item.description: Taking your vitamins with your morning coffee can quietly erase most of what you paid for — iron absorption can drop by half or more. This evidence-based guide covers exactly which supplements coffee interferes with, which ones it leaves alone, and the simple timing fix.

item.title: Itchy Skin But No Rash? The Nutrient Tests Worth Asking About
item.description: An itch that crawls under your skin with no rash is easy to dismiss, but it is sometimes linked to a measurable nutrient gap, and low iron is the best-documented one. This guide covers which blood tests to ask your doctor about, what the evidence does and doesn't show, and how a confirmed deficiency is usually treated.

item.title: Best Iron Supplement That Won't Upset Your Stomach: The Gentle Forms and Dosing That Actually Work
item.description: Iron pills leaving you nauseated and constipated? The best iron supplement that won't upset your stomach is usually a matter of form and timing. This evidence-based guide covers ferrous bisglycinate, alternate-day dosing, and exactly what to buy.

item.title: Best Supplements for Muscle Recovery After a Workout: What the Research Actually Supports
item.description: Sore for three days after leg day? This evidence-based guide ranks the best supplements for muscle recovery after a workout — creatine, protein, omega-3, tart cherry, and curcumin — with real dosages, timing, and honest evidence grades so you only buy what works.

item.title: Vitamin B12 Deficiency Symptoms and Supplements: The Tingling, Fatigue, and Brain Fog You Keep Blaming on Everything Else
item.description: Vitamin B12 deficiency hides behind ordinary tiredness until the nerve damage starts — and by then some of it can be permanent. This evidence-based guide covers the real symptoms, who is at risk, how it is diagnosed, and exactly which B12 supplement form and dose actually fixes it.

item.title: Turmeric vs Curcumin Supplement: What You Are Actually Paying For (2026 Evidence Review)
item.description: Turmeric and curcumin are not the same thing, and the difference decides whether your supplement does anything at all. We break down the turmeric vs curcumin supplement question — bioavailability, the right dose, which conditions the research actually supports, and the liver-safety news you need before you buy.

item.title: Supplements for Menopause Symptoms: What the Evidence Actually Supports in 2026
item.description: A no-hype, evidence-graded guide to supplements for menopause symptoms — hot flashes, sleep, mood, and bones. We rank black cohosh, soy isoflavones, magnesium, vitamin D, melatonin, and ERr 731 with the meta-analyses to back them, and call out the popular pills that do nothing.

item.title: Best Probiotics for Bloating: Which Strains Actually Work (2026 Evidence Review)
item.description: Not all probiotics reduce bloating — most do nothing. We rank the specific strains (B. infantis 35624, L. plantarum 299v, B. lactis HN019, and more) with real RCT evidence, explain who should skip probiotics entirely, and tell you exactly what to buy.

item.title: Best Supplements for Hair Growth in Women: What the Evidence Actually Says (2026)
item.description: Iron, vitamin D, zinc, biotin, marine collagen, saw palmetto, pumpkin seed oil — we rank every popular hair-growth supplement for women by evidence quality, explain who actually needs them, and tell you exactly what to buy.

item.title: Ashwagandha vs Rhodiola for Stress: Which Adaptogen Wins in 2026?
item.description: Ashwagandha and Rhodiola rosea are the two most-studied adaptogens for stress — but they work on different parts of the stress response. We break down the meta-analyses, head-to-head trials, dosing, and exactly which one to choose for chronic stress, burnout, or performance under fatigue.

item.title: Best Supplements for Joint Pain Over 50: What the 2024 Meta-Analyses Actually Show
item.description: Glucosamine, collagen, curcumin, omega-3, Boswellia — the joint supplement aisle is a wall of competing claims. We pulled the most recent meta-analyses and randomized trials to rank what actually works for knee and hip pain after 50, what dose to take, and which combinations have the strongest evidence.

item.title: Fish Oil vs Krill Oil: What the 2024 Network Meta-Analyses Actually Show
item.description: Krill oil costs 3–5x more than fish oil and the marketing pitch is "better absorbed." We pulled the most recent network meta-analyses to see whether the bioavailability story holds up, and which omega-3 actually wins on triglycerides, inflammation, and price-per-gram of EPA+DHA.

item.title: Do Collagen Supplements Actually Work? A 2026 Evidence Review
item.description: Collagen powders are a $2B category, but the science is messier than the marketing. Here is what recent meta-analyses actually show for skin, joints, hair, and bones — and how to pick a product that does what it claims.

item.title: Multivitamin vs. Individual Supplements: Why One Pill Isn’t Enough (and When It Is)
item.description: A multivitamin is a generic seatbelt; individual supplements are targeted treatments. Here’s the evidence on dose, form, and absorption — and when a multi actually makes sense.

item.title: Natural Supplements for Anxiety: What the Science Actually Says
item.description: Looking for natural supplements for anxiety? This evidence-based guide ranks the top 6 options — ashwagandha, L-theanine, magnesium, lavender, and more — by clinical evidence strength, with exact dosages and what to buy.

item.title: Vitamin D3 vs D2: Which Form Actually Works Better?
item.description: Wondering whether to take vitamin D3 or D2? Research shows D3 raises blood levels up to 3x more effectively than D2. This evidence-based guide breaks down the science, dosages, and exactly which form to buy.

item.title: Best Supplements for Gut Health: What the Science Actually Says (2026)
item.description: From probiotics to butyrate, discover the best supplements for gut health ranked by clinical evidence. This research-backed guide covers dosing, strain selection, and exactly which supplements are worth your money.

item.title: Zinc vs Magnesium: Which Mineral Do You Actually Need?
item.description: Zinc and magnesium are two of the most commonly deficient minerals in adults — but they do completely different things. This research-backed comparison breaks down the benefits, deficiency signs, dosage, and who should take zinc vs magnesium (or both).

item.title: Supplements for Runners Over 40: The Evidence-Based Guide to Training Harder and Recovering Faster
item.description: Running after 40 means fighting harder biology: slower recovery, joint wear, and declining muscle mass. This evidence-graded guide covers the best supplements for runners over 40 — what actually works, what to skip, and exactly how to dose each one.

item.title: Creatine vs Protein Powder: Which One Is Right for Your Goals?
item.description: Creatine and protein powder both build muscle — but they work completely differently. This evidence-graded breakdown tells you exactly which to prioritize, how to dose each, and why serious athletes use both.

item.title: Best Magnesium for Sleep: The Science-Backed Guide to Forms, Dosage, and Timing
item.description: Not all magnesium supplements work the same for sleep. This deep-dive compares magnesium glycinate, L-threonate, citrate, and more — with dosage recommendations backed by clinical trials.

item.title: What Supplements Should I Take? A Personalized, Evidence-Based Guide
item.description: With thousands of supplements on the market, deciding what to take can be overwhelming. Here's a systematic, evidence-based approach to figuring out exactly what your body needs.

item.title: Best Supplements for Energy: The Evidence-Based Guide
item.description: Persistent fatigue and low energy are among the most common reasons people reach for supplements. Here's what the research actually shows works — and what's just marketing.

item.title: Top Supplements for Sleep: What Science Says Actually Works
item.description: Sleep problems affect over a third of adults. These supplements have solid clinical trial data supporting their effectiveness for sleep onset, sleep quality, and duration.

item.title: How Your Diet Shapes Your Supplement Needs
item.description: Your dietary pattern is the single strongest predictor of which nutrients you're likely deficient in. Here's what each major diet gets right — and where the gaps are.

item.title: Vitamin D Deficiency: Signs, Testing, and How to Fix It
item.description: A billion people worldwide are deficient in vitamin D — and most don't know it. Learn to recognize the signs, understand your risk factors, and know exactly when and how to supplement.

item.title: Supplements for Brain Fog: What the Evidence Shows
item.description: Brain fog — that feeling of mental cloudiness, slow thinking, and poor concentration — has several root causes. Here are the supplements with the best evidence for clearing it.

item.title: The Science of Personalized Supplements: Why One Size Doesn't Fit All
item.description: Why does your friend swear by iron while it does nothing for you? Why do vegans need different supplements than omnivores? The science of nutritional individuality explains why personalization isn't optional — it's everything.

item.title: Magnesium Benefits: The Complete Evidence Guide
item.description: From sleep quality and stress resilience to heart health and blood sugar regulation, magnesium is involved in over 300 enzymatic reactions. Here's a comprehensive look at the science behind every major benefit.

item.title: Vitamin D3: Why 70% of People Are Deficient (And What to Do About It)
item.description: Despite being called a vitamin, D3 functions more like a hormone — influencing over 200 genes. Here's the science on deficiency, optimal levels, and supplementation.

item.title: Magnesium: The Master Mineral for Sleep, Stress, and Recovery
item.description: Involved in over 300 enzymatic reactions, magnesium may be the single most impactful supplement for modern lifestyles. Here's why most people don't get enough.

item.title: The Science Behind Ashwagandha: Does It Actually Work?
item.description: KSM-66 ashwagandha has accumulated impressive clinical trial data for stress, cortisol, and even testosterone. We review the evidence.

item.title: Creatine Is Not Just for Bodybuilders — The Brain Benefits Are Compelling
item.description: The most evidence-backed sports supplement also shows remarkable benefits for cognition, mood, and neuroprotection. Here's what the research says.

item.title: Omega-3 for Vegans and Vegetarians: The Complete Algae Oil Guide
item.description: Fish don't actually make omega-3 — they get it from algae. Here's why algae oil is the superior choice for plant-based eaters (and arguably everyone).
